tools.description:
Read a context suggestion and one page of evidence and proposed changes from its latest review. Use a suggestion id returned by the suggestions list or a known suggestion. Follow nextCursor with the same suggestionId until it is null, even when sources is empty. Each page contains at most 10 sources and up to 10 proposals of each updateType in proposedChanges. unavailableSourceCount counts evidence withheld on this page. Evidence contents require access to their source threads. If the review changes or a cursor is invalid, omit cursor to restart. Re-list if the suggestion is unavailable. When latestReview is RUNNING, empty update lists do not mean there are no proposed changes; read again later without a cursor. Read reviewCoverage before claiming which evidence the review used. File payload.diff may be partial: join fragments by proposal id and diffOffset, following nextCursor until diffLength is reached before applying a patch. Offsets and lengths count UTF-16 code units. File proposals include applyReadiness, or applyUnavailableReason when their target is missing or inaccessible. For file conflicts, repeat the same page with previewProposalId set to that file proposal's id. Preview contents are bounded: follow applyPreview.nextCursor as previewCursor, keeping the same proposal id and suggestion cursor. tools.description:
Cancel the CURRENT open publication review after explicit user approval. No review-ID binding exists. Cancellation does not roll back metadata already saved by preview/update/publish, and does not unpublish an existing publication. Obtain explicit user approval through the MCP host before invoking this tool. The host owns its approval policy; the server cannot independently verify a human decision. Do not invoke based only on inferred intent. After an uncertain response, stop and read get_project_publication to observe current state. There is no per-operation receipt or automatic replay guarantee; do not blindly repeat a publication mutation. The private working-project name, public publication title (settings.name), and URL slug (settings.slug) are distinct; never infer a title or slug change from a working-project rename. For a share-link request, preserve any existing slug; prepare a nonempty URL-safe slug in the proposal only when absent or when the user requests a URL change, before approval and verify public_url after completion. show_canvas does not establish whether chats are hidden; no separate chat-privacy control or complete composition inventory is available, so do not promise that chats are excluded. Pending moderation runs automatically: wait and read state; only awaiting_confirm needs a separate flagged-item decision. Capture can include changes made while publication is in flight; after a completed snapshot, later working-project changes require republishing. Report completion only from observed state and review, never merely an accepted mutation response. For republish, compare snapshot_id and processing state with the prior observation. An unchanged snapshot may be a successful no-op when current content is already served, or the old version while work is in flight; do not infer pending from an unchanged ID. tools.description:
Search already-created Elements in one Elements library: the project selected by scope, otherwise the caller's personal library, which is strictly My Elements. Returns compact IDs, names and state; read details with elements_get. Never use this to find project assets, uploads, generation jobs or ordinary folders. operation=projects discovers accessible Elements libraries only; authors/properties discover filters in the selected library; operation=folders lists its Elements folders. Do not guess IDs or permissions.

USAGE IN GENERATION:
Embed `<<<element_id>>>` inside `params.prompt` of `generate_image` / `generate_video`. Backend auto-injects the image and rewrites to `@element_name`. Multiple placeholders per prompt OK.
Example: `"Cinematic portrait of <<<UUID>>> on a rooftop"`, `"<<<A>>> handing coffee to <<<B>>> in a Paris cafe"`.

SUPPORTED MODELS (`params.model` = machine name, friendly in parens):
- Image: `gpt_image_2_6` (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst), `gpt_image_2_6_flare` (GPT Image 2.6 Flare), `nano_banana_pro` (Nano Banana Pro), `nano_banana_2` (Nano Banana 2), `gpt_image_2` (GPT Image 2), `seedream_v4_5` (Seedream 4.5), `seedream_v5_lite` (Seedream 5.0 lite), `cinematic_studio_2_5` (Cinema Studio Image 2.5).

USER-FACING STYLE: prefer friendly model names and element names for readability.

- `@name` form does NOT work in tool calls — only `<<<UUID>>>` in `params.prompt`.

- `kling3_0` only honors reference elements when an explicit `start_image` is provided in `params.medias`. Save publication metadata and prepare Cinema preview data. This does not open a rendered preview; only report a link if one is actually returned. This is a MUTATION and may immediately change existing public metadata. First read current settings and disclose the effective resulting prompts/canvas/discovery visibility for user approval. A published project returns its current snapshot, not a private frozen republish draft. Obtain explicit user approval through the MCP host before invoking this tool. The host owns its approval policy; the server cannot independently verify a human decision. Do not invoke based only on inferred intent. After an uncertain response, stop and read get_project_publication to observe current state. There is no per-operation receipt or automatic replay guarantee; do not blindly repeat a publication mutation. The private working-project name, public publication title (settings.name), and URL slug (settings.slug) are distinct; never infer a title or slug change from a working-project rename. For a share-link request, preserve any existing slug; prepare a nonempty URL-safe slug in the proposal only when absent or when the user requests a URL change, before approval and verify public_url after completion. show_canvas does not establish whether chats are hidden; no separate chat-privacy control or complete composition inventory is available, so do not promise that chats are excluded. Pending moderation runs automatically: wait and read state; only awaiting_confirm needs a separate flagged-item decision. Capture can include changes made while publication is in flight; after a completed snapshot, later working-project changes require republishing. Report completion only from observed state and review, never merely an accepted mutation response. For republish, compare snapshot_id and processing state with the prior observation. An unchanged snapshot may be a successful no-op when current content is already served, or the old version while work is in flight; do not infer pending from an unchanged ID.
